title: Using the same box again and again
idea: Once a variable holds a value, you can use it in many lines. Store once, reuse as often as you like.

exercises.prompt:
What does this show?

name = 7
print(name)
print(name)
options: 7 on one line, then 7 on the next line
exercises.explanation: The box still holds 7, so each print(name) shows 7. Reusing a variable gives the same value each time.

exercises.prompt: After you store a value in a variable, you can print it more than once.
exercises.explanation: Yes! Store it once, then use it as many times as your program needs.

exercises.prompt:
What does this show?

score = 20
print(score)
print("Great!")
print(score)
exercises.explanation: Lines run top to bottom: the value 20, then the text Great!, then the value 20 again.

exercises.prompt: The value stored in a variable stays the same each time you read it (in this unit). So print(count) twice shows...
options: a bigger value the second time
exercises.explanation: Reading a box doesn't change it. Same value every time you print it.

exercises.prompt: The variable pet holds a value. Build a SECOND line to show it again (a copy of print(pet)).
exercises.explanation: print(pet) shows the stored value. Writing it again shows the same value again.

exercises.prompt:
What does this show?

stars = 3
print(stars)
print(stars)
print(stars)
exercises.explanation: The box holds 3 the whole time, so every line shows 3. Reuse keeps the same value.

exercises.prompt: Printing a variable uses up its value, so the second print shows nothing.
exercises.explanation: No — printing just looks inside the box. The value stays, so you can print it again and again.

exercises.prompt: Put these lines in order: store a value, show it, then show it once more.
exercises.explanation: Fill the box first, then read it twice. Each read shows 5.

exercises.prompt: Why is it handy to store a value in a variable instead of typing it each time?
options: You write the value once and reuse the name everywhere
exercises.explanation: One source of truth. Store it once, use the name as many times as you like.

exercises.prompt:
What does this show?

gift = 9
print("Your number:")
print(gift)
exercises.explanation: The text line shows first, then print(gift) shows the stored value 9.
